normalisation.width: cross-section resampled onto u=(y-c)/sigma over [-3,3] in 48 bins; every response vector divided by its own mean
normalisation.opacity: profile rescaled to mean 1.0; grain histogram over ratio a/meanInk in 25 bins; ink response divided by its own mean

axes.profile: width- and opacity-normalised cross-section shape (48 bins, mean absolute difference)
axes.grain: opacity-normalised ink density histogram (25 bins over r = a/meanInk), compared by earth-mover distance in r units — total variation saturates on smooth brushes whose histogram is a near-delta
axes.direction: effective width at 0/45/90/135 deg, divided by its own mean (chisel vs round)
axes.size: effective width at pressure 0.2/0.45/0.7/0.95, divided by its own mean
axes.ink: mean ink at those pressures, divided by its own mean

method.gate: per pair, per axis: clamp(1 x max(scalarResidual(a), scalarResidual(b)), pooledResidual.p10, pooledResidual.p95). A pair is a duplicate only when ALL five axes are inside their gate — the conjunction, not any single axis, carries the precision.
method.clustering: cliques, not connected components: a brush joins a cluster only if it is a duplicate of every member already in it

noiseFloor.source: same brush re-rendered with the two knobs the owner named actually turned: strokeWidth 16 -> 24 and opacity 1.0 -> 0.7 (plus a sub-pixel path offset). Whatever distance survives normalisation here is what 'only the numbers differ' measures like, per brush.
